links.outcome: Clinician-rated quality of LLM vs human therapist responses across five quality dimensions
links.effect: Ratings were similar on a 1-5 scale, e.g. overall quality LLM 4.00 vs human 3.96 (d=0.06); empathy LLM 4.31 vs human 4.08 (d=0.42); helpfulness LLM 3.85 vs human 3.93.
links.quote: LLM-generated responses were judged to be of comparable quality to those written by human therapists, though qualitative feedback indicated they were at times generic and insufficiently challenging.

links.outcome: Clinician perception of tone, empathy and appropriateness of LLM-generated therapeutic responses
links.effect: LLM responses had higher empathy ratings (4.31 vs 4.08, d=0.42), but qualitative feedback described them as generic and at times excessively empathetic. Raters identified the LLM source correctly 63% of the time.
links.quote: Qualitative analysis indicated that LLM-generated responses were perceived as polished but also generic and at times excessively empathetic.

screen.reason: The study is an empirical experiment evaluating LLM-generated responses compared to human responses in simulated iCBT scenarios using blinded clinician ratings, but it does not test a specific deployment practice or guardrail.
